title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
source: curated summary - authentic text at the India Code URL

sections.heading: Arbitration agreement
sections.text: An agreement to submit present or future disputes to arbitration. It must be in writing, which includes an exchange of communications or pleadings in which existence is alleged and not denied.

sections.heading: Power to refer parties to arbitration
sections.text: A judicial authority before which an action is brought in a matter covered by an arbitration agreement shall refer the parties to arbitration unless it finds prima facie that no valid agreement exists.

sections.heading: Interim measures by court
sections.text: A party may apply to court for interim measures before or during arbitral proceedings, or after the award but before enforcement.

sections.heading: Appointment of arbitrators
sections.text: Where parties fail to appoint under the agreed procedure, the Supreme Court or High Court, or a person or institution designated by it, makes the appointment, confining itself to the existence of the agreement.

sections.heading: Competence of arbitral tribunal to rule on its jurisdiction
sections.text: The kompetenz-kompetenz principle: the tribunal may rule on its own jurisdiction, including on the existence or validity of the arbitration agreement, which is treated as separable from the main contract.

sections.heading: Commencement of arbitral proceedings
sections.text: Unless otherwise agreed, proceedings commence on the date the request to refer the dispute to arbitration is received by the respondent. Relevant to limitation.

sections.heading: Time limit for arbitral award
sections.text: The award in a domestic arbitration is to be made within twelve months from completion of pleadings, extendable by six months by consent and thereafter only by the court.

sections.heading: Application for setting aside arbitral award
sections.text: The only recourse against an award. Grounds are narrow: incapacity, invalid agreement, want of notice, matters beyond the scope of submission, irregular composition, non-arbitrability, or conflict with the public policy of India. Must be filed within three months, extendable by thirty days on sufficient cause and no further.

sections.heading: Appealable orders
sections.text: Appeals lie from orders refusing to refer to arbitration, granting or refusing interim measures, and setting aside or refusing to set aside an award.
